output.title: Retrieval quality is a workflow constraint
output.body:
If an AI tool has to look things up to do useful work, retrieval quality is part of the workflow design. Simple version: when the system searches documents, email threads, FAQs, or past records, it has to pull back the right material consistently, or the answer looks neat and is still wrong. That means rework for you, or a confident mistake you now have to unwind.

For a small business owner, the question is not “can AI answer this?” It is “can it find the right source every time this task runs?” A useful rule of thumb is to look at one recurring task that already makes you search more than one place for the answer. Customer questions, invoice checks, and lead follow-up are all fair examples.

Before you automate that workflow, audit the source material for that one task. Are the documents named clearly, grouped sensibly, and kept current? If the inputs are messy, automation usually moves the manual work earlier instead of removing it.

One control to keep is source display: the system should show which document it used before you trust the answer. Bareni’s self-built local knowledge-assistant demo shows grounded answers with sources on synthetic data, but the public route is locked, so treat that as a demo pattern, not a deployed service. The practical next step is plain: pick one repeating workflow and check whether the information is organised well enough to retrieve before you try to automate it.
